messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Follow-up: Quinova hosting & air-gap qualification — key constraints and next steps

Hi Janette / Nathan —

Thanks again for the 45-minute walkthrough today. Quick recap from our side and suggested next steps so we stay aligned: 

Summary of pain & goals
- Regulatory driver: patient data classification (PHI) requires strict egress controls and auditability; objective is to run inference for read/triage workflows inside Quinova-controlled boundaries.
- Air-gap preference: procurement & legal said they'd prefer an air-gapped/on-prem option for certain regions, with an initial pilot in the Boston data center.
- Network constraints: no outbound traffic to public endpoints from the inference cluster; only outbound to a narrow set of management IPs via customer-managed jumpbox is allowed.
- SLAs: target p95 latency <300ms for 4k token requests; throughput 30 req/s during peak hours.

Technical constraints we heard (please confirm if I missed anything)
- Inbound: Quinova will allow connections from the private control plane over a customer-managed VPN (IPsec) but only via a bastion; no direct internet-facing endpoints allowed.
- Egress: all telemetry, metrics, and kernel updates must route through the bastion and be logged to the customer SIEM; no direct S3 egress from the inference nodes.
- Key management: customer KMS/HSM in-scope; Redwood must support envelope encryption with customer KMS.
- Air-gap cadence: quarterly maintenance windows preferred; any emergency patching requires pre-approved access window.

Attachments: attached the list of SOC2/security questionnaire items we referenced (quinova-soc2-questions.xlsx) and a quick topology sketch (network-topology-sketch.png).

Proposed next steps
1) We will prepare a short technical runbook that maps Redwood Private components to your bastion/VPN flow and call out required firewall rules. Delivery: Tue 2027-02-16.
2) Nathan / Quinova infra to share a simple CIDR/IP allowlist and preferred bastion host details. Delivery: by EOD Wed 2027-02-17.
3) Procurement to confirm target SOW/PO cadence — Ben, can we get a draft commercial outline for a 6-month pilot?

If that matches your understanding, we can schedule a 30-minute follow-up to align on the runbook details. Thanks again — felt like good momentum.

—
Evelyn Hart
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference

Evelyn —

Thanks for the clear recap; that mostly matches what we discussed. A few clarifications / additions:
- Confirmed: pilot will be air-gapped in our Boston facility and we will not allow direct egress to public S3 buckets.
- We will require local log forwarding to our Splunk cluster (not to a Redwood-hosted service).
- Upgrade cadence: we are ok with quarterly maintenance for non-critical patches. Emergency security fixes will be handled via the approved jumpbox access process you outlined.

Action items on our side:
- Nathan will share the bastion IP + preliminary CIDR by 2027-02-17.
- Procurement will review the pilot SOW and come back with preferred billing terms (net 45) by 2027-02-19.

One ask: before the runbook, can you confirm whether Redwood supports running the model weights inside the customer VPC and never uploading weights to your control plane? We need to state that clearly for our auditors.

Hi Janette / Nathan —

Quick update: attached runbook draft (summary tab of what will be in the full runbook) is in our internal doc; below are the high-level answers to immediate auditor questions: 

- Will model weights ever be stored in Redwood-managed object storage? No — for the air-gapped pilot we will keep model artifacts on customer-managed storage inside the VPC/on-prem appliance. Redwood control plane will store only metadata necessary for job orchestration and encrypted pointers; no plaintext weights will leave customer environment.

- KMS/HSM integration: Redwood supports envelope encryption where the data key is wrapped by the customer KMS. We can integrate with common cloud KMS services and on-prem HSMs (PKCS#11); our security team will run an integration checklist with your Nathan.

- Logs / telemetry: inference nodes can forward structured logs to your Splunk endpoint over the bastion; we will not send raw logs to Redwood-hosted logging unless explicitly configured in a later phase.

Next steps (short timeline)
- Thu 2027-02-18: Redwood delivers full runbook + firewall rule set.
- Wed 2027-02-17: Quinova shares bastion details and CIDR (Nathan).
- By 2027-02-19: Procurement to confirm terms; Ben to circulate draft SOW the same day.

If that looks good I can schedule the runbook walk-through for Friday morning (PST).

Best,
Evelyn
